interpretation.benign-perturbations: an expectation about the policy; a failure here is a finding, and is kept
interpretation.published-conditions: a gate on this harness; a failure here means the harness is wrong

policy.evaluated_by: numpy reimplementation of stable_baselines3.SACPolicy.predict; torch is not a run-time dependency
policy.evaluation: deterministic mean action, tanh-squashed then unscaled to the action box
policy.feature_extractor: CombinedExtractor (parameter-free: flatten + concat in sorted key order)

alternatives_considered.why_not_primary: trained on FetchPickAndPlace-v1 (the mujoco-py environment, no longer installable) and behind sb3_contrib's TimeFeatureWrapper, so running it needs both an environment-version transplant and a wrapper reimplementation, and its published mean_reward was measured on an environment that cannot be run here — it cannot serve as a check on this harness
trained on the right environment version, but publishes only best_model.zip with no config and no eval protocol, so there is less to pin and nothing to reproduce
published mean_reward -12.70 +/- 12.81; the spread implies failed episodes at nominal

licence.note_on_the_environment: the SCENE is a different matter and is properly licensed: Gymnasium-Robotics is MIT (Farama Foundation), and the Fetch MJCF it ships carries that licence
licence.status: NOT DECLARED by the model repository
licence.survey: Every FetchPickAndPlace checkpoint found on the hub declares no licence: the six that were checked one by one (IntelliGrow/FetchPickAndPlace-v4, sb3/tqc-FetchPickAndPlace-v1, hhmm1122/fetch-pickandplace-sac-her, crislmfroes/tqc-FetchPickAndPlace-v2, Edgar404/td3-FetchPickAndPlaceDense-v2-v3, qgallouedec/tqc-FetchPickAndPlace-v1-3795610126) all have no license field, no license tag and no LICENSE file. This is the same position the humanoid target reached for Humanoid policies, and it is reported rather than papered over.
licence.what_this_project_does: the weights are downloaded at run time and are NOT vendored, redistributed or modified; only their sha256 digests and the measured behaviour are published as evidence

reproduces_published_number.note: the publisher's number is their claim over 10 unspecified deterministic episodes; this is a check that the numpy actor, the observation key order and the compatibility shim reproduce the published behaviour, not an independent evaluation of the policy

results.name: published-conditions-seed-0
results.why_it_must_not_drop: the environment and the policy exactly as published; anything but a placement is a harness fault

results.name: published-conditions-seed-1
results.why_it_must_not_drop: same, a second block and goal placement

results.name: lighter-part
results.why_it_must_not_drop: half the published block mass; a gripper that can hold 2 kg should hold 1 kg

results.name: slightly-slicker-grip
results.why_it_must_not_drop: 30 % less grip friction; still far above the coefficient of a dry hand on plastic

results.name: part-1cm-off
results.why_it_must_not_drop: the part 1 cm from where the environment put it, a fifth of the block's own width

results.name: a-little-actuation-noise
results.why_it_must_not_drop: 5 % of the action half-range of zero-mean noise, well inside any real servo's jitter
